subject: Question on bootstrap procedure in mediation analysis

messages.author: 5aeb8bfc1b46dfd8
messages.subject: Question on bootstrap procedure in mediation analysis
parts:
Hi there,

I have a question regarding the bootstrapping in mediation analyses.
Is the bootstrapping procedure used for all paths, so a, b, c, c' and the indirect path, or only for calculating the indirect path?

Thank you in advance for your answer!

Best wishes
Charlotte van 't Westende

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Question on bootstrap procedure in mediation analysis
parts:
Charlotte,

It's most important for the indirect path, because the product of coefficients has an asymmetric sampling distribution. So tests and CIs based on multipliers of standard errors will be off.

For individual coefficients, if all assumptions are met, bootstrapped CIs and normal-theory CIs, will be asymptotically equivalent. In most practical cases, there's no downside to using the bootstrap for all the CIs if you're using it anyway for the indirect.

Pat
